voice_style: Professional cinematic documentary narrator (British or neutral English)

segments.text: Over twelve thousand kilometres apart. Two nations. One war, over a few windswept islands.
segments.delivery: Strong, low opening hook; slight pause after 'apart' and after 'nations'

segments.text: The Falklands, called Las Malvinas in Argentina, lie about 480 kilometres off its coast. Britain has ruled them since 1833.
segments.delivery: Calm, informative; let 'Las Malvinas' land clearly

segments.text: On 2 April 1982, Argentina invaded the Falklands. A day later, it seized South Georgia.
segments.delivery: Build tension; short beat before 'A day later'

segments.text: Britain sent a task force south on 5 April. By 26 April, South Georgia was back under British control.
On 21 May, British troops landed at San Carlos, then advanced across East Falkland towards Stanley.
On 14 June, Argentine forces in Stanley surrendered. The war had lasted 74 days.
segments.delivery: Slow down on 'surrendered'; pause before '74 days'

segments.text: 649 Argentine and 255 British servicemen died, along with three islanders.
segments.delivery: Measured, respectful, no drama in the numbers

segments.text: In 2013, 99.8 percent of islanders voted to stay British.
Argentina still claims the islands. Britain says the islanders decide. More than four decades on, the dispute is not settled.
segments.delivery: Slow, weighty finish; long pause before the last sentence
